review_evidence: The three primary Lean files comprise ACLibrary, its segment-tree implementation, and Main.lean, which imports the library and defines tropical-monoid conversions, parser helpers, instances, and an executable segment-tree program.
Direct inspection of Main.lean shows substantive Lean definitions and executable logic rather than a documentation/build wrapper.

With only three primary files and distinct roles for the library entrypoint, data structure, and executable example, no exact-path exclusion can be justified without losing formal or implementation prior art.

review_evidence: Verified the single path from the brief exists under reservoir-sources/zer0-star__lean-ac-library.

Read the file in full: `structure Segtree (alpha : Type) [Monoid alpha] (n : Nat)` with well-formedness invariant `WF`/`WF'`, plus 31 named declarations forming the standard segment-tree API (construction, point update, range fold, invariant-maintenance lemmas) via `grep -n '^def\|^private def\|^lemma\|^theorem\|^structure\|^abbrev\|^instance\|^example'`.

summary: Surveyed the checkout (reservoir-sources/zer0-star__lean-ac-library): confirmed the single review-list file exists. This source is a Lean formalization of AtCoder Library data structures; the prior review RRV-2453b656f568-r1's summary 'Retain the AC library, segment-tree implementation, and executable checked example' names this exact file's content. Byte size via `wc -c`: ACLibrary/Segtree.lean 10950. Read the file in full: it defines a monoid-based segment tree, `structure Segtree (alpha : Type) [Monoid alpha] (n : Nat)`, with a well-formedness invariant `Segtree.WF`/`Segtree.WF'` (internal nodes equal the product of their children), then builds up the full standard segment-tree API and its correctness proofs: `mk`, `updateAt`/`updateAt_WF'`, `build'`/`build` (bottom-up construction with a well-founded recursion proof), `get`/`get_eq_get'`, two `GetElem` instances, `WF_without`/`WF_without_WF`/`WF_WF_without_zero`/`WF_without_set`/`WF_without_updateAt` (invariant-maintenance lemmas), `Vector.buildAt`, `set`/`modify`, `get_updateAt_ne`/`buildAt_keep_larger`/`get_set_self`/`get_set_ne` (point-update correctness), `fold_all`/`fold_aux`/`fold`/`fold_naive`/`fold_naive_one` (the range-fold operation and a naive reference implementation), `leftmost`/`leftmost_lower`/`leftmost_upper`, and the file's capstone `theorem fold_eq_fold_naive (t : Segtree alpha n) (l r : Nat) ... : t.fold l r = t.fold_naive l r`, proved in full (case split on l=r, then `fold_aux_eq_foldr`/`fold_naive` rewriting and `simp`) -- a genuine, complete correctness proof that the efficient O(log n) fold matches its O(n) naive specification. Declaration-keyword grep confirms 40 matches across 31 named declarations (structures, abbrevs, defs, lemmas, theorems, instances). Ran `\bsorry\b`, `\badmit\b`, and `TODO|FIXME|XXX` greps over the file: zero matches for all three patterns -- every proof is complete. Genuine, complete formal data-structure content; no exclusions.
